description: One-off grammar and semantic corners: LIMIT NULL means no limit (with OFFSET, over the streaming WHERE+LIMIT path, and on a FROM-less select); a bare DESCRIBE is refused while DESCRIBE TABLE works qualified or not; INSERT OVERWRITE INTO truncates first while the TABLE spelling is refused; ALTER SESSION SET applies every comma-separated assignment; USE SECONDARY ROLES takes a role list; a dollar-quoted column COMMENT; DATE_PART refusing the FROM form; a star function argument parsing (leaving an unknown function a runtime gap, not a grammar one); the VALUES alias inside the parens; FLATTEN over a bare subquery; USING joins merging the column while both sides stay addressable; UPDATE accepting FROM before SET; the curly-brace star select item with EXCLUDE / ILIKE / qualified forms and its source-form column label; TEMPORARY FILE FORMAT; and a CHANGES window whose END point lies in the future. Converted 1:1 from features/SyntaxBreadthSingletonsTest (now retired); the ALTER SESSION test skips snowflake as the Java class did and reads the applied values back through SHOW PARAMETERS instead of the engine's session context. One divergence from the Java class: it granted the two roles to CURRENT_USER, whose name it interpolated into the DDL; a JSON step cannot interpolate, and CURRENT_USER here is the OS account name, so the converted test grants to a user it creates and drops itself - the assertions (every statement accepted, the session still usable) are unchanged.
